detail.readme:
# free-email-domains [![Last version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/microlinkhq/free-email-domains?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/microlinkhq/free-email-domains/releases) [![NPM Status](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/free-email-domains?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/free-email-domains) > Free and disposable email domains in a single list, validated against DNS every day. ## Highlights - **30,000+ domains.** Free providers (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook and thousands of regional ones) and disposable providers (Mailinator, Temp Mail and the like) together. - **Six sources plus a curated list.** Merged, deduplicated and lowercased. - **Validated against DNS.** A domain is removed when its DNS records say it cannot receive email. - **Updated every day.** A new version is published whenever the list changes. - **Zero dependencies.** It is a JSON array of strings, with TypeScript types. ## Why use it - Block temporary or throwaway inboxes during signup. - Tell personal emails from work emails to qualify leads. - Reduce fake form submissions. - Keep CRM and email workflows cleaner. ## Install ```bash $ npm install free-email-domains --save ``` ## Usage The module exports an array of lowercase domains: ```js const freeEmailDomains = require('free-email-domains') freeEmailDomains.includes('gmail.com') // => true freeEmailDomains.includes('mailinator.com') // => true freeEmailDomains.includes('your-company.com') // => false ``` It works the same with ES modules: ```js import freeEmailDomains from 'free-email-domains' ``` ### Checking an email address Create a `Set` once to get constant time lookups, then compare the part after the last `@` in lowercase: ```js const freeEmailDomains = new Set(require('free-email-domains')) const isFreeEmail = email => { const domain = email.slice(email.lastIndexOf('@') + 1).toLowerCase() return freeEmailDomains.has(domain) } isFreeEmail('hello@gmail.com') // => true isFreeEmail('Hello@Mailinator.com') // => true isFreeEmail('hello@your-company.com') // => false ``` Domains are matched exactly: `gmail.com` is listed, `mail.gmail.com` is not. ### Without Node.js The list is a plain JSON file, so any language can use it: ```bash $ curl -sL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/free-email-domains/domains.json ``` ## How the list is built The list is rebuilt every day from these sources: - [HubSpot free domains](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/forms/what-domains-are-blocked-when-using-the-forms-email-domains-to-block-feature) – free email providers. - [castle/disposable-email-domains](https://github.com/castle/disposable-email-domains) – disposable providers. - [disposable-email-domains/disposable-email-domains](https://github.com/disposable-email-domains/disposable-email-domains) – disposable providers. - [groundcat/disposable-email-domain-list](https://github.com/groundcat/disposable-email-domain-list) – disposable providers, MX validated. - [7c/fakefilter](https://github.com/7c/fakefilter) – disposable providers observed in the wild. - [unkn0w/disposable-email-domain-list](https://github.com/unkn0w/disposable-email-domain-list) – disposable providers. - A curated list of providers missing from the sources above, at [scripts/sources.mjs](scripts/sources.mjs). Then every domain coming from a source is checked against DNS, asking two public resolvers (Cloudflare and Google): | DNS answer | Result | | --- | --- | | It has MX records | kept | | It has no MX records but it has an A or AAAA record ([implicit MX](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5321#section-5.1)) | kept | | It publishes a [null MX](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7505) | removed | | It does not exist, or it has no MX, A or AAAA record | removed | | Timeout or server failure | unchanged from the previous scan | A domain is only removed when both resolvers agree it cannot receive email. Removed domains are stored at [inactive-domains.json](inactive-domains.json), and they come back on the first daily scan where a resolver finds them accepting email again. The scan refuses to write anything when a resolver fails a sanity check (`gmail.com` must be active, a `.invalid` name must not exist), or when too many domains come back inactive or unanswered. Curated domains are never removed by the scan. Domains listed by a source that are neither free nor disposable providers are excluded with the allowlist at [scripts/sources.mjs](scripts/sources.mjs). ## Update data Fetch the sources, scan DNS and write `domains.json` and `inactive-domains.json`: ```bash $ npm run update ``` The scan takes about a minute. The `postinstall` script does the same without the DNS scan, reusing `inactive-domains.json`: ```bash $ node scripts/postinstall.mjs ``` ## Contributing - Missing a provider? Add it to `DOMAINS` at [scripts/sources.mjs](scripts/sources.mjs). - Is a legit business domain listed? Add it to `ALLOWLIST` at [scripts/sources.mjs](scripts/sources.mjs). ## Related - [email-providers](https://github.com/derhuerst/email-providers) – Top 3k common emails by Alexa rank. ## License **free-email-domains** © [Microlink](https://microlink.io), released under the [MIT](https://github.com/microlinkhq/free-email-domains/blob/master/LICENSE.md) License.
